Flu: Rest at home, stay hydrated, take paracetamol for fever. Consult a doctor if symptoms persist beyond 3 days.
COVID-19: Isolate, monitor oxygen levels, stay hydrated, take paracetamol for fever. Seek medical attention if breathing difficulty occurs.
Pneumonia: Antibiotics if bacterial, rest, fluids, and fever reducers. Hospitalization may be required for severe cases.
Asthma: Use prescribed inhaler, avoid triggers, seek emergency care if severe shortness of breath.
Bronchial Asthma: Use prescribed inhaler, avoid triggers, seek emergency care if severe shortness of breath.
Diabetes: Monitor blood sugar, take prescribed medication, maintain healthy diet and exercise.
Hypertension: Take antihypertensive medication, reduce salt intake, regular exercise, monitor blood pressure.
Chickenpox: Rest, calamine lotion for itching, keep skin clean, avoid scratching blisters.
Chicken pox: Rest, calamine lotion for itching, keep skin clean, avoid scratching blisters.
Malaria: Take antimalarial drugs as prescribed, rest, stay hydrated, seek medical care for complications.
Typhoid: Antibiotics, rest, drink plenty of fluids, eat soft foods, maintain hygiene.
Tuberculosis: Long-term antibiotics, regular follow-up, good nutrition, avoid spreading infection.
Food Poisoning: Drink fluids, rest, avoid solid foods until vomiting stops, seek medical care if severe.
Allergy: Avoid allergens, take antihistamines, use nasal sprays for congestion, consult doctor for severe reactions.
Migraine: Lie down in a dark room, apply cold compress to forehead, take ibuprofen. Avoid triggers like bright lights.
Sinusitis: Steam inhalation, saline nasal spray, pain relievers, antibiotics if bacterial.
Otitis Media: Pain relievers, warm compress, antibiotics if bacterial, consult doctor for persistent symptoms.
Conjunctivitis: Use lubricating eye drops, avoid touching eyes, antibiotics if bacterial, maintain eye hygiene.
Psoriasis: Moisturize skin, use medicated creams, avoid triggers, consult dermatologist for severe cases.
Guillain-Barre Syndrome: Hospitalization, supportive care, physical therapy, immunotherapy as prescribed.
Jaundice: Treat underlying cause, rest, avoid alcohol, maintain hydration, consult doctor for persistent symptoms.
Fungal Infection: Use antifungal creams or medications, keep affected area dry, maintain hygiene.
Fungal infection: Use topical or oral antifungal medication as prescribed; keep the area dry and clean. See doctor if spreading.
Common Cold: Gargle salt water for sore throat, use over-the-counter decongestants, rest and drink fluids.
GERD: Avoid spicy and fatty foods, eat small frequent meals, use antacids or proton-pump inhibitors as advised by a doctor.
Chronic cholestasis: Manage underlying liver condition with a specialist, monitor liver function, and follow medical treatment and lifestyle advice.
Drug Reaction: Stop the suspected drug and seek medical attention. Antihistamines or corticosteroids may be given depending on severity.
Peptic ulcer diseae: Proton-pump inhibitors and antacids, avoid NSAIDs and smoking; test and treat H. pylori if present.
AIDS: Begin antiretroviral therapy under specialist care, regular monitoring, and supportive treatment for opportunistic infections.
Gastroenteritis: Maintain hydration with ORS, follow a bland diet, rest; seek medical care for high fever or persistent vomiting/diarrhea.
Dengue: Stay hydrated, rest, use paracetamol for fever, avoid NSAIDs; seek urgent care for bleeding or severe abdominal pain.
hepatitis A: Supportive care, rest, avoid alcohol; hepatitis A vaccine prevents infection.
Hepatitis B: Consult a hepatologist; antiviral therapy if indicated, vaccination prevents infection.
Hepatitis C: Consult specialist; antiviral treatment is available and effective for most cases.
Hepatitis D: Requires management by a hepatologist; often occurs with hepatitis B co-infection.
Hepatitis E: Supportive care and hydration; severe cases need medical attention, especially in pregnancy.
Alcoholic hepatitis: Stop alcohol immediately, nutritional support, and specialist care; medications as advised by a hepatologist.
Dimorphic hemmorhoids(piles): High-fiber diet, stool softeners, sitz baths, topical treatments; surgical options for severe cases.
Heart attack: Call emergency services immediately; aspirin (if not contraindicated) and urgent hospital care are essential.
Varicose veins: Compression stockings, leg elevation, regular exercise; consult vascular specialist for procedural options.
Hypothyroidism: Thyroid hormone replacement therapy and regular monitoring by an endocrinologist.
Hyperthyroidism: Beta blockers for symptoms, antithyroid medications, and specialist follow-up; definitive treatments may include ablation or surgery.
Hypoglycemia: Consume fast-acting glucose (juice, glucose tablets), recheck blood sugar, seek urgent care for severe or recurrent episodes.
Osteoarthristis: Weight management, low-impact exercise, analgesics, physiotherapy; consider injections or surgery for severe cases.
Arthritis: Anti-inflammatories, physical therapy, disease-specific treatment (rheumatologist) depending on the type of arthritis.
(vertigo) Paroymsal Positional Vertigo: Epley maneuver or vestibular rehabilitation exercises; avoid sudden head movements and consult ENT if persistent.
Acne: Topical retinoids, benzoyl peroxide, or oral antibiotics for moderate cases; isotretinoin for severe nodular acne under dermatologist care.
Urinary tract infection: Appropriate antibiotics as prescribed, increased fluid intake, and urinary hygiene; see doctor if recurrent.
Impetigo: Topical or oral antibiotics as prescribed, keep lesions clean and covered to prevent spread.
